fields.title: What to Do When the Budget Does Not Add Up
fields.keyTakeaway: When the budget does not add up, first drop from the path, move in time, and precompute, and only then optimize—because reducing work is cheaper than speeding it up.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: The sum of minimum possible times exceeds the goal. What now?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: This is a common situation, and without a structured response it turns into endless optimization or silently dropping the goal. Four levers resolve it faster than trying to speed up everything.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: When the budget does not add up, there are four moves, and three of them are product moves.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: **Drop from the path.** Something on the screen does not have to be there. Recommendations, counters, optional blocks. The cheapest move, and it requires a product decision.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **Move in time.** Show the screen without some data, load it later. Works if the user starts interacting before the data is needed.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **Precompute.** Calculate in advance instead of on-demand. A materialized view from `DS2-N1-L2`, cache, night recalculation.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: **Optimize.** The most expensive move and the last in line.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: The order is not random: the first three change the amount of work, the fourth changes execution speed. Reducing work is almost always cheaper than speeding it up.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: Separately—**revising the goal.** Sometimes 1.5 seconds was chosen arbitrarily, and 2 seconds is no worse. Checked with data: drop-off by wait intervals, like in the `PF1-G-B` gate.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: What not to do: silently accept an unreachable goal. A goal that no one intends to meet devalues all others.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Checkout screen: goal 3 s, minimum possible time unchanged—4.2 s.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: *Dropped from path:* promo code check when there is no promo code (180 ms), recommendations call for a removed block (140 ms). 320 ms for free.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: *Moved in time:* calculation of bonuses earned for the order—shown after confirmation. 260 ms.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: *Precomputed:* available delivery slots used to be calculated on demand, now recalculated every 5 minutes in the background. 640 ms.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: *Left to optimize:* combining 12 stock check calls into one. 420 ms.
fields.sections/3/blocks/5/text: Total 4.2 → 2.56 s, of which only the last item was an optimization. Three-quarters of the gain came from decisions on what to do and when.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Moving in time creates intermediate states, and they require design per `IN1-N4-L2`. Saving milliseconds at the cost of a jumping UI is a bad trade.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: When the budget does not add up, first drop from the path, move in time, and precompute, and only then optimize—because reducing work is cheaper than speeding it up.
